newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent a lb higher to 0.100 lower while feeder cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent a lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Some analysts cited the current large discount of futures to cash cattle prices and strong choice boxed beef market as supportive factors. Choice cattle supplies are tight as many are being sold ahead of schedule, they said.
Lightweight choice boxed beef prices rose to $115.14 per cwt late Friday, the highest level since April 19, 1994. Select beef prices were again lower.

However, other analysts again cited expectations of falling cash cattle prices. Projections are for increased cattle numbers coming to market by December and demand for beef is expected wane soon seasonally, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to climb following a fairly large advance in the latest CME feeder cattle index. This should offset expectations of steady to higher corn futures prices, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.37 at $63.85 per cwt, the highest level since October 3.
Agricultural futures markets will close early at 1200 CST due to the Veterans Day holiday.
